To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) kernel-mode malware can exploit the dynamic nature of kernel data to evade previous solutions, (2) the kernel-mode malware can be detected by mapping the kernel object to a data structure and checking the integrity of this data structure, and (3) we can map kernel object to data structures by using the object's type and the offset of its members

we have identified 28% of dynamic kernel data that are not covered by existing kernel integrity solutions, and we have developed a novel technique that can systematically cover 100% of the dynamic data, and thus provide a more effective solution for kernel integrity checking.

kernel-mode malware may manipulate function pointers and other dynamic data to evade detection, that previous solutions may fail to protect against such attacks, and that our approach, called Dynamic Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization (DKASLR), can detect such attacks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following two problems: 1) how to systematically identify all the kernel objects that are mapped to dynamic kernel data; and 2) how to efficiently map the identified kernel objects to dynamic kernel data.
the following questions: (1) What is the size of the dynamic kernel memory? (2) What is the coverage of the current kernel integrity solutions?
the following two questions: 1) What is the extent of kernel integrity checking? 2) Can we achieve better protection?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the existing solutions for checking kernel data integrity can only reach 28% of all dynamic kernel objects and therefore may not be able to identify all malware.
the current kernel integrity checking solutions have not yet reached the point where they could be considered as reliable protection mechanisms against kernel-mode malware.
the current state of the art is not sufficient for the protection against kernel-mode malware, and that there is a clear need for a new approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a systematic way to map kernel objects to their memory regions.
we propose a new kernel integrity solution that is based on a novel kernel mapping scheme and a novel kernel integrity checking mechanism.

we have designed a new kernel object model and implemented it in the form of a kernel module, called KOM, which is a kernel object model that maps kernel objects to a new data structure called kernel object graph.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to systematically map kernel objects to their corresponding kernel data structures and then use the mapping to systematically inspect dynamic kernel data.
it is feasible to map kernel objects and their dynamic data to a virtual memory address space.
kernel objects are a promising source of information to systematically check kernel integrity.
